posts.title: Standards-Compliant 112G PHY for Linear Optics: Driving Efficient AI Infrastructure
posts.summary:
112G PHY IP for linear optics to reduce power, latency and thermal load for high-speed data movement in AI and data center systems.
The post Standards-Compliant 112G PHY for Linear Optics: Driving Efficient AI Infrastructure appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Synopsys has introduced a 112G PHY IP compliant with the OIF-CEI-112G-LINEAR-PAM4 standard, designed to enable DSP-less host-to-module connectivity.
Adopting linear optics can reduce module power consumption by up to 50% by eliminating the need for power-hungry DSPs and retimers in AI data center racks.
The solution addresses critical thermal and latency bottlenecks, providing a scalable pathway for future interconnect speeds of 224G, 448G, and Co-Packaged Optics (CPO).
Standardization of the linear drive interface ensures interoperability across the ecosystem, which is essential for the rapid scaling of high-density AI infrastructure.

posts.title: 2D GAA CFETs Need Contact And Parasitic Co-Optimization At A2 Node (imec)
posts.summary:
Researchers from imec published a technical paper titled “Are Gate-All-Around 2D CFETs the Optimal Architecture for the A2 Node and Beyond?” Abstract Excerpt: “Here, we develop an A2-oriented 2D CFET integration flow with a CPP of 36 nm and Lg of 10 nm and present initial demonstrations of several key process modules. Despite their atomically... » read more
The post 2D GAA CFETs Need Contact And Parasitic Co-Optimization At A2 Node (imec) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Imec research indicates that 2D Gate-All-Around (GAA) CFETs do not offer a contacted poly pitch (CPP) scaling advantage over traditional Si GAA CFETs at the A2 node.
The study establishes a minimum CPP of 36 nm for 2D CFETs, constrained by contact formation requirements despite the use of atomically thin channels.
Effective implementation of 2D CFETs at the A2 node requires rigorous co-optimization of contact structures and parasitic extraction to realize potential power-performance-area (PPA) benefits.
The findings utilize a comprehensive multiscale evaluation framework, including quantum transport simulations and circuit-level benchmarking, to assess the viability of 2D architectures.

posts.title: Scaling AI agents with trustworthy data
posts.summary: Business and technology leaders need no convincing that the time of agentic AI is here. Organizations are rapidly adopting agents, and few executives doubt the technology’s potential to transform work. But many organizations find that realizing the desired return on investment (ROI) from AI hinges on having the right foundation, with inadequate infrastructure and data…
bullets: Enterprise adoption of agentic AI is currently bottlenecked by legacy data infrastructure, which struggles to provide the real-time, cross-functional access required for autonomous decision-making.
Data leaders currently provide AI agents access to over 70% of enterprise data, whereas the average organization limits agents to just 45%, significantly impacting ROI and performance.

With Gartner predicting that AI agents will automate or augment 50% of business decisions by 2027, firms must modernize data architectures to ensure agents have the context and reliability needed for high-stakes operations.

The shift from passive AI chatbots to active, agentic systems necessitates a transition from siloed legacy systems to unified data environments that support frictionless, secure operational integration.

posts.title: Scientists just created female clones of male mice
posts.summary: Scientists have deliberately turned male mouse embryos into females for the first time. A team based in Japan used a CRISPR-based approach to remove the Y chromosome from male cells and create female clones of male mice.  “No one has done this before,” says Monika Ward, a reproductive biologist at the University of Hawaii, who…
bullets: Researchers in Japan have successfully used a CRISPR-based technique to remove the Y chromosome from male mouse embryos, effectively creating female clones from male cells.
While currently in the preprint stage, this breakthrough challenges the biological assumption that both male and female gametes are strictly required for mammalian reproduction.

The technology holds significant potential for wildlife conservation, offering a pathway to rescue endangered species by managing sex ratios or preserving genetic diversity when only male individuals remain.

This development builds on previous observations of sex-reversal in nature, such as the Okinawa rubble goby, and could eventually refine current, inefficient cloning methods used for species like black-footed ferrets.

posts.title: Xiaomi EV delivers 31,267 units in July, 39% of annual target
posts.summary:
Xiaomi EV needs average monthly deliveries of nearly 67,000 units over the remaining 5 months to achieve its full-year target of 550,000 units.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Xiaomi EV delivered 31,267 vehicles in July, marking the fourth consecutive month above the 30,000-unit threshold despite a 9.99% month-on-month decline.
The company has achieved only 39% of its 550,000-unit annual delivery target, necessitating a significant production ramp-up to an average of 67,000 units per month for the remainder of the year.
Xiaomi is pivoting toward the extended-range electric vehicle (EREV) market with its new Sky Nomad series, positioning the N90 Max and N70 Max to compete directly with Li Auto and Aito.

While initial market reaction to the Sky Nomad pricing was negative, causing a 7.28% drop in Xiaomi's stock, early reports suggest strong consumer interest with potential pre-orders exceeding 100,000 units.
